newsitem.title: MEXICO: British investors eyeing Mexico's airports.
newsitem.headline: British investors eyeing Mexico's airports.

text.p: A mission of British business leaders is planning to visit Mexico next week to talk about opportunities to invest in Mexico's airport privatization, the British embassy said on Wednesday.
Led by the president of the British Airport Group, Gil Thompson, the mission will meet in Mexico's second largest city from July 21-25 for a seminar on privatization opportunities.

"Mexico has the most developed airport infrastructure in Latin America with a network of 83 airports," the embassy said in a statement. It called the privatization the world's largest airport sale to private hands.

Mexico has still not officially presented its plan to sell off its largest airports, but has said it will privatize them in regional blocks later this year. The privatization has been repeatedly postponed.
